summary: Goffstown, NH lookout on the Uncanoonuc Mountains: a warden's station in 1925, closure announced in 1937 pending repairs; listed as gone and removed, with no build or removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by FireLookout.org and marked removed on Forest Lookouts; no removal date found in the sources read

access.note: Wikipedia describes the mountains as still a good spot for hiking and snowshoeing; the sources read do not state who owns the summit

visit.trail_note: The former incline railway on the South Peak is now a hiking trail; no source describes any remains of the lookout

events.note: George E. Flanders, forest fire warden at Uncanoonuc, died in January 1925; a Portsmouth Herald obituary describes his lookout station on the mountain top
The State Department of Forestry and Recreation said the Mt. Uncanoonuc lookout would close after repair work in progress was finished
A fire damaged the incline railway that served the South Peak ski operation; this concerns the railway, not the lookout

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no build date, tower height or design appears in any source read, and no removal date is given. The Forest Lookouts page gives its lookout as on the mountain without naming a peak; the NH Family Hikes list names South Uncanoonuc Mountain, which the story follows. The Goffstown Historical Society Facebook posts (one on a 1926 replacement tower, one on the hotel fire) could not be read, so nothing from them is used. The 1941 railway fire is in the facts as context only. The brief record (tower, gone) is consistent with the sources; no corrections proposed. No photos added: the Commons image shows the hotel, not the lookout.
